title: SymmetricAlgebraSheafConstruction
statement: For a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme] and an $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], define the presheaf $P(U)=\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X(U)}F(U)$, with restrictions extending module restriction by the symmetric algebra universal property [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. Define $S=P^\#$ under $\mathcal O_X$ using the sheafification unit [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], define $\theta_U:P(U)\to S(U)$ as this unit, and define the linear map $j:F\to S$ by $j_U(x)=\theta_U(\iota_U(x))$.

source.place: Modules, Section 01CF (section-symmetric-exterior, line 3262: definition of Sym(F) as a quotient of the tensor algebra), Lemma 01CG (lemma-local-tensor-algebra, line 3303: Sym^n F is the sheafification of U -> Sym^n_{O(U)}(F(U))), Lemma 01CL (lemma-whole-tensor-algebra-permanence, line 3461: Sym of a quasi-coherent module is quasi-coherent); Schemes, Section 01LA item (9) (schemes.tex line 4717); used as Sym^*_{O_X} in Properties, Lemmas 05JS, 086N, 0817

proof_origin.place: Modules, Section 01CF and Lemmas 01CG, 01CH, 01CL (definition of Sym(F) as the sheafification of U ↦ Sym_{O(U)}(F(U)), quasi-coherence, proofs omitted or sketched); Schemes, Lemma 01I8; Algebra, Lemma 0C6F. The universal property and the affine-section argument are written by the agent from these.
